title: Six hundred thousand batteries at Monolith
text: At the Monolith substation here, Southern California Edison switched on a battery in 2014 built out of 608,832 lithium-ion cells. It held 32 megawatt-hours and could deliver 8 megawatts, enough to run between 1,600 and 2,400 houses for four hours. When it was switched on it was the largest lithium-ion battery system running in North America, and it lasted eight years before it was shut down in 2022.

s1.title: Tehachapi Energy Storage Project
s1.quote: The Tehachapi Energy Storage Project ... is an 8MW/32MWh lithium-ion battery-based grid energy storage system at the Monolith Substation of Southern California Edison (SCE) in Tehachapi, California. ... The TSP system is constructed of 608,832 lithium-ion battery cells ... At the time of commissioning in 2014, it was the largest lithium-ion battery system operating in North America ... could power between 1,600 and 2,400 homes for four hours ... operated successfully for eight years before formal decommissioning in 2022.

s2.title: Monolith, California
s2.quote: In 2014, Southern California Edison commissioned the Tehachapi Energy Storage Project at Monolith Substation, the largest lithium-ion battery system operating in North America at the time.
